title: Monotonicity after adding a squared coordinate
statement: Let $n$ be a dimension, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube $\{0,1\}^n$, and let $d\in\mathbb R$. If the closed Gaussian profile at the expectation of $f$ is at most the Bobkov functional of $f$, then $\sqrt{\overline I(\E[f])^2+d^2}\le\sqrt{B(f)^2+d^2}$, where $\overline I$ denotes the closed Gaussian profile and $B(f)$ the Bobkov functional.
hypotheses_covered: closed Gaussian profile at $\E[f]$ is at most $B(f)$
replaced: For a real function $f$ on the uniform Boolean cube $\{0,1\}^n$, write $D_i f(x)=(f(x^{i\leftarrow0})-f(x^{i\leftarrow1}))/2$ and $B(f)=\mathbb E\sqrt{\overline I(f)^2+\sum_i(D_i f)^2}$, where $\overline I$ is the Gaussian profile extended by zero outside $(0,1)$. If $d\in\mathbb R$ and $\overline I(\mathbb E f)\le B(f)$, then $\sqrt{\overline I(\mathbb E f)^2+d^2}\le\sqrt{B(f)^2+d^2}$.
